title: You Actually Share Your Brain With a Silent Stranger
beats: Your brain is two halves; crossed wiring; the connecting wire can be cut as epilepsy treatment
Post-split patients seem normal, except the left hand disagrees with the right over outfits
Restate the model: each half sees/controls opposite side; only left brain speaks
Experiment: show word to right brain only; speaking brain says it saw nothing
Right hand picks the object; left brain invents a confident wrong reason
Confabulation isn't lying; healthy people do it too, and you have
More experiments: can't name object in hand; draws two objects at once
Who is 'you'? Speaking half vs the half that hears and answers; face recognition lives on the right
Why doesn't the right brain freak out after separation?
Flagged speculation: right brain was always a separate mind that resigned once speech took over
Two of you are watching this video right now; your objection is what left brain would do
Speculation aside: at minimum there is a separate something that hears and responds
'You is two' then handoff to Kurzgesagt collab

new_moves.name: new:rule-restatement-before-test
new_moves.what: Re-state the exact minimal model immediately before the experiment that depends on it

new_moves.name: new:objection-as-evidence
new_moves.what: Predicts the viewer's disbelief and reframes it as proof of the theory
new_moves.evidence: 3:58 arguing is exactly what talking left brain would do

new_moves.name: new:speculation-fence
new_moves.what: Explicitly brackets speculative section with entry and exit markers

theory: Grey installs a two-rule model (crossed control, speech only on the left) in 40 seconds, then runs a sequence of literally staged experiments the viewer can predict from those rules. Because the model is tiny and stable, each new experiment costs no new symbols, and the escalation moves from perception to identity. He then fences off speculation so the confident tone never contaminates what is established.
velocity: Scene builder: two-pane split stage where each half has its own visibility mask; experiments are just changing which pane gets the stimulus
Orchestrator: restate the minimal rule set right before each test beat that depends on it
Voice: mark speculation with explicit enter/exit phrases so the learner model tags claims as established vs conjectural
Evals: after 2 experiments, ask learner to predict the third's outcome before revealing it
quote: Who is you? You is two.
